tasks.author: ai-task-writer-a
tasks.prompt: Summarise what the Rail primary must and must not do when the duplicate capture alert fires.

rubric.text: It starts as a SEV1 and stays SEV1 until shown that no cardholder was charged twice; declare first, then investigate.
Never replay, retry or re-send captures, refunds or payouts by hand or by script.
On-call does not void or refund anything, single or bulk; collect the affected payment IDs and hand them to the Payments Ledger team, who refund with finance operations.
Merchants are told within 2 hours of the incident being declared, through the template; Rail does not contact cardholders.
The DuplicateCaptureSuspected alert may never be silenced, not even briefly during a deploy.

tasks.notes: cross-section: Severity levels, Safety rules, Dashboards and alerts, the double charge playbook and Open questions.

tasks.author: ai-task-writer-a
tasks.prompt: Summarise when on-call may evacuate a region and how an evacuation is carried out.

rubric.text: It needs the engineering manager on call to agree; the primary runs it, and only one evacuation can be in progress.
Traffic moves in steps of 25%, with at least 3 minutes between steps.
Evacuating West does not bring card payments back if the problem is the token vault or its region link; the vault team must confirm the problem is elsewhere.
Moving back needs the same steps and agreement, and not in the same shift unless the region has been healthy for at least 2 hours.
Not when both acquirers are failing (no traffic shifts then); evacuation stays allowed during the change freeze.

tasks.notes: cross-section: Region evacuation, the both-acquirers playbook and the change freeze.
